question: You find an abandoned elderly woman in a village with no food or medical care. What is the best way to coordinate her care?

options.A: Connect her with local social welfare agencies and senior support programs
options.B: Tell her neighbors to handle it completely on their own
options.C: Wait until the federal health budget is reviewed next year
options.D: Admit her to the maternity ward for routine antenatal checks

explanation: You're thinking like a true nurse! Your role includes acting as a bridge, linking vulnerable patients directly to the social services and agencies equipped to help them long-term.

question: Why is learning about infectious agents so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: To diagnose rare genetic disorders in newborns
options.B: To prevent widespread disease outbreaks in populations
options.C: To replace the need for environmental sanitation workers
options.D: To manufacture antibiotics in local health centers

explanation: Spot on! When you understand how these tiny germs behave, you can help protect your entire community from getting sick. Great nursing insight!

question: Which ethical principle gives a client the right to make their own healthcare choices?

options.A: Negligence
options.B: Maleficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Autonomy is the ethical principle that respects an individual's right to self-determination and personal decision making without outside control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: When is the right time to apply suction during tracheostomy suctioning?

options.A: While pushing the catheter down into the airway
options.B: Continuously throughout the entire procedure
options.C: Only while withdrawing and rotating the catheter
options.D: Before inserting any tubing into the stoma

explanation: Never apply suction on the way in! You only suction gently while twisting and pulling the catheter out to protect the delicate airway lining.

question: A hormone travels through the whole body, but why does it only affect certain cells?

options.A: Non-target cells actively destroy the hormone on contact
options.B: The blood only carries the hormone toward specific organs
options.C: Target cells are the only ones physically close to endocrine glands
options.D: Target cells possess specific receptors that bind to that hormone

explanation: Hormones are like keys floating around, but they only fit into matching locks (receptors) on their specific target cells. Neat, right?

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain ramps up electrical activity during a seizure?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Glutamate

explanation: Spot on! Glutamate is the main 'gas pedal' neurotransmitter that drives excessive brain cell firing during a seizure.

question: Why must a nurse know the specific type of FGM a patient has experienced?

options.A: It determines the appropriate legal fine for the family
options.B: It dictates the patient's future career choices
options.C: It guides the exact surgical and obstetric management needed
options.D: It predicts the exact age when the procedure was done

explanation: Spot on! Different types involve different levels of tissue removal, which tells you what kind of clinical care or surgery she might need. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h1)

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations
options.B: By producing antibodies after surviving a childhood illness
options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: Why do heart infections cause different symptoms depending on which layer of the heart is involved?

options.A: Pathogens can only survive within the muscular layer of the heart.
options.B: Only the outermost layer contains pain receptors, masking infections in other areas.
options.C: Different layers are composed of entirely separate blood supplies that never interact.
options.D: Each heart layer performs a distinct structural and functional role, leading to varied symptoms when inflamed.

explanation: Think about what each layer does—the inner lining handles valves, the middle pumps, and the outer protects. Naturally, when a specific layer gets sick, the signs will match its unique job!

question: Why is treating only the physical wounds of a rescued trafficking victim not enough?

options.A: The psychological and social scars require extensive care
options.B: Mental health issues are never linked to physical trauma
options.C: Physical wounds always heal completely on their own
options.D: Physical treatment is too expensive for local clinics

explanation: Trafficking leaves deep emotional scars and isolation, meaning these children need dedicated mental health support alongside medical care.

question: Why does a healthy woman usually handle the blood loss of childbirth without going into shock?

options.A: Her platelet count drops to zero to prevent any fluid movement
options.B: Her total blood volume expanded significantly during pregnancy
options.C: Her bone marrow stops all red blood cell production temporarily
options.D: Her heart rate drops to zero during every single uterine contraction

explanation: Remember all that extra volume she built up over nine months? It acts as a safety buffer so she handles delivery blood loss like a champ.

question: When changing sheets for a bedridden patient who cannot get up, how should you handle the top covers?

options.A: Place the clean top sheet over the old one, then pull the old sheet out from underneath
options.B: Ask the patient to hold the dirty blanket up with both hands
options.C: Remove all covers completely, leaving the patient uncovered until the end
options.D: Strip the top of the bed first and replace sheets while the patient sits up

explanation: Spot on! Layering the clean cover over the old one before sliding the old one out keeps your patient warm and protects their privacy the whole time.

question: Why are people with long-term HIV at a higher risk for heart disease?

options.A: Patients universally develop severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Low red blood cell counts force the heart to beat faster
options.C: Persistent systemic inflammation damages blood vessels
options.D: The virus directly destroys heart muscle tissue daily

explanation: Ongoing immune activation keeps the body in a state of low-level inflammation, which over time can damage blood vessels and raise heart disease risk.

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in treating medical waste?

options.A: Freezing body tissues for long-term storage
options.B: Crushing glass bottles into fine reusable sand
options.C: Sterilizing infectious items using high-pressure steam
options.D: Dissolving expired pharmaceutical tablets in acid

explanation: Correct! Autoclaves use high heat and steam to kill off pathogens before the waste leaves the facility.

question: Which service is a key part of disease prevention in comprehensive health care?

options.A: Performing major open-heart surgeries
options.B: Giving routine immunizations to children
options.C: Importing expensive specialized drugs
options.D: Building high-rise luxury hospitals

explanation: Immunizations stop preventable infectious diseases from spreading through a community, making them a core preventive service. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: Why is hypertension frequently described as a silent condition?

options.A: It causes severe pain only at night
options.B: It only affects people who cannot speak
options.C: It disappears on its own without treatment
options.D: It damages blood vessels without causing early symptoms

explanation: High blood pressure often develops over years without any noticeable warning signs, which is why regular checks are necessary. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of leadership compared to management in nursing?

options.A: Policy enforcement
options.B: Inventory control
options.C: People and vision
options.D: Budgeting and schedules

explanation: While management handles systems and operations, leadership focuses primarily on guiding people and inspiring a shared vision for care. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for tele-nursing practice in developing regions?

options.A: Erratic electricity supply and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Patients refusing to use phones for any medical reason
options.C: An overabundance of advanced video monitoring equipment
options.D: Excessive physical contact between nurses and clients

explanation: Unreliable power and weak network signals frequently interrupt remote healthcare delivery in resource-constrained settings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: A patient reports hot flashes, night sweats, and irregular cycles. Which body systems are these complaints linked to?

options.A: Endocrine and reproductive systems
options.B: Musculoskeletal system
options.C: Gastrointestinal system
options.D: Respiratory system

explanation: You've got this! Hot flashes and night sweats happen when estrogen levels shift, which ties directly back to our hormone (endocrine) and reproductive systems.

question: What is a major danger of leaving a needle stuck inside a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: It automatically dilutes the concentration of the liquid drug
options.B: It allows environmental pathogens to enter and contaminate the medicine
options.C: It increases the expiration date of the remaining medicine
options.D: It causes the rubber stopper to dissolve completely into the solution

explanation: Leaving a needle sitting in a vial creates an open doorway for bacteria and viruses to sneak in and multiply. Always remove the needle after drawing up your dose!

question: A pregnant woman's tummy measures bigger than expected for her gestational age. What should you, as the nurse, expect next?

options.A: Immediate induction of labor due to suspected term delivery
options.B: An ultrasound scan to check for multiples or other causes
options.C: Restriction of fluid intake to reduce amniotic volume
options.D: Discharge from antenatal care with reassurance

explanation: Correct! A 'large-for-dates' fundal height is a classic clinical clue. Ordering an ultrasound helps us check if there are twins, extra fluid, or if the dates just need tweaking.

question: Why is having a blood transfusion service so important in a CEmOC facility?

options.A: To reduce the incidence of newborn jaundice following difficult deliveries
options.B: To prevent mild gestational anemia during routine antenatal clinic visits
options.C: To speed up cervical dilation during the active phase of normal labour
options.D: To replace severe blood loss from conditions like postpartum hemorrhage or placenta previa

explanation: When a mother loses too much blood, quick access to safe blood can literally mean the difference between life and death.

question: A patient asks for the best protein choice on a low-fat diet. What do you recommend?

options.A: Ribeye steak with visible marbling
options.B: Skinless chicken breast and white fish
options.C: Pork sausage links fried in oil
options.D: Deep-fried chicken wings with skin

explanation: Skinless poultry and white fish are naturally lean and low in fat compared to red meats or fried options.

question: What is the clock-face method used for during mealtime assistance?

options.A: Measuring the exact caloric content of each food portion
options.B: Describing the spatial location of food items on a plate
options.C: Checking the temperature of hot liquids before serving
options.D: Timing how fast the patient finishes eating their meal

explanation: The clock-face method (e.g., 'your rice is at 6 o'clock and chicken at 12 o'clock') helps visually impaired patients locate their food and eat independently.

question: In the Three Delays model, what does the 'first delay' stand for?

options.A: Delay in arriving at the hospital due to bad roads
options.B: Delay in receiving treatment from doctors
options.C: Delay in diagnosing the pregnancy
options.D: Delay in deciding to seek medical care

explanation: The first delay happens right at home or in the community—when family members take too long to recognize danger signs or hesitate to go to the hospital.

question: How does poor food purchasing directly affect patient outcomes?

options.A: It improves the patient's appetite significantly
options.B: It always results in immediate food poisoning
options.C: It decreases the overall cost of hospital stays
options.D: It can lead to nutrient deficiencies and health complications

explanation: Sourcing poor quality or inadequate food items deprives the body of essential nutrients needed for recovery and maintenance. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: Why doesn't the mother's immune system treat the growing fetus like a foreign invader and attack it?

options.A: The mother's immune system turns off completely during pregnancy.
options.B: The placenta uses special mechanisms to suppress local maternal immune responses.
options.C: Fetal cells disguise themselves as maternal liver cells.
options.D: The fetus has no white blood cells to trigger an immune reaction.

explanation: Fascinating, right? The placenta acts like a peacekeeper, creating a special low-immune zone so the mother's body doesn't reject the baby.

question: Why is emotional distress often addressed alongside physical pain in palliative nursing?

options.A: Hospital policies mandate psychological screening before any pain medication is given
options.B: Psychological symptoms are always easier to treat than somatic sensations
options.C: Emotional worry can worsen how a patient feels and experiences physical pain
options.D: Physical analgesics work exclusively by altering brain chemistry related to mood

explanation: The mind and body are closely linked, meaning anxiety, depression, and fear can amplify a patient's perception of physical discomfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h1)

question: Why is blood typing and crossmatching ordered right away for a patient with heavy post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: To check for chronic viral infections
options.B: To figure out how many weeks pregnant she was
options.C: To have matching blood ready for an emergency transfusion
options.D: To find out if she is allergic to IV fluids

explanation: Heavy bleeding drops blood volume fast, so having matched blood on standby is a lifesaver. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: What happens to the nerve in a mild injury called neurapraxia?

options.A: The axon stays intact while the myelin sheath suffers temporary damage
options.B: The blood supply to the nerve is permanently cut off, causing rapid cell death
options.C: Both the axon and the outer connective tissue sheaths are completely severed
options.D: The axon is crushed or cut while the outer connective tissue tube stays intact

explanation: Neurapraxia is just a temporary block—like a pinched nerve. The myelin takes a little hit, but the core axon stays safe and sound.

question: As a nurse, why would you advise a patient not to smoke on the morning of their barium meal test?

options.A: Smoking increases stomach acid and gut movement
options.B: Nicotine stains the inside of the X-ray machine
options.C: Smoking causes the barium mixture to curdle
options.D: Nicotine interferes with the water-soluble dye

explanation: Spot on! Nicotine wakes up the stomach, making extra juices and movements that can blur the pictures we need. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which specific cells inside the testes make testosterone?

options.A: Leydig cells
options.B: Germ cells
options.C: Sertoli cells
options.D: Brunner cells

explanation: Leydig cells are the hardworking factories inside the testes that pump out testosterone whenever they get the signal from the brain!

question: Why does lower kidney function in older adults increase their risk of drug overdose or side effects?

options.A: Reduced urine production causes the bladder to dissolve pills
options.B: The kidneys start producing extra enzymes that break drugs down
options.C: Older kidneys absorb all pills directly into the bloodstream
options.D: Medications are cleared from the body much more slowly

explanation: Spot on! When kidneys slow down, they take longer to flush out medications, causing drugs to build up in the system and reach toxic levels.

question: What is the very first thing you should do when someone asks you a drug-related question?

options.A: Consulting a tertiary drug reference textbook
options.B: Formulating the final verbal response for the doctor
options.C: Searching the primary medical literature for clinical trials
options.D: Securing demographic and background data about the patient and requester

explanation: Spot on! Before you can hunt for an answer, you need to know who is asking and the patient's specific health situation.

question: Why do some clinics continue to use outdated clinical practices instead of modern guidelines?

options.A: Strict orders from international health ministries
options.B: Requests made directly by pregnant women
options.C: Scientific proof that old methods work better
options.D: Habit and resistance to changing traditional routines

explanation: Spot on! Old habits die hard in healthcare. This is why keeping up with continuous education is so important for modern nurses.

question: A patient is scheduled for a surgical procedure on both legs requiring complete lower body numbness without general anesthesia. Which route of administration is the surgical team most likely to select?

options.A: Subcutaneous
options.B: Intrathecal
options.C: Intramuscular
options.D: Transdermal

explanation: Spinal anesthesia delivered intrathecally provides rapid, profound regional anesthesia for lower body surgeries. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the single best way to stop infections from spreading in any healthcare setting?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns for every procedure
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Using disposable plastic trays

explanation: Simple handwashing or alcohol rubbing is your superpower against hospital infections. It removes germs picked up from patients and surroundings instantly.

question: How do drugs like metronidazole mainly kill protozoa?

options.A: By disrupting DNA synthesis inside the parasite cell
options.B: By stimulating the human immune system to attack
options.C: By dissolving the outer cell wall using strong acids
options.D: By blocking the absorption of dietary calcium

explanation: Spot on! Metronidazole enters the parasite and creates reactive compounds that damage its DNA, stopping it from multiplying.

question: What does a patient's drug history cover?

options.A: Prescriptions, OTC items, herbs, and supplements
options.B: Surgical history and previous hospital admissions
options.C: Only traditional and cultural remedies used at home
options.D: Only prescription drugs prescribed by a doctor

explanation: A complete drug history covers every substance a patient takes, including hospital drugs, chemist items, herbs, and local supplements. You've got this!

question: Which patient is the best candidate for a soft diet?

options.A: A client diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia
options.B: A patient running a high fever from malaria
options.C: A person recovering from dental surgery
options.D: An individual with severe kidney failure

explanation: Patients with healing mouths or missing teeth need soft foods that do not require heavy chewing. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h2)

question: Which dangerous practice is often triggered by a shortage of disposable syringes?

options.A: Reusing disposable syringes or improper sterilization
options.B: Refusing to treat patients who arrive without insurance
options.C: Giving all medications exclusively through oral tablets
options.D: Storing vaccines at room temperature for weeks

explanation: Severe supply shortages often force facilities to reuse single-use equipment, drastically increasing infection rates. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge faced by NGOs working in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural resistance and suspicion from community elders
options.B: Heavy reliance on unstable international donor grants
options.C: Excessive, guaranteed long-term funding from secure local taxes
options.D: Insecure terrain and poor rural road networks

explanation: NGOs don't collect taxes! In fact, relying on unpredictable donor grants is one of their biggest headaches, not a guaranteed income.

question: Why is family planning counseling important early in the postpartum period?

options.A: Traditional birth control methods never work after childbirth
options.B: Women cannot get pregnant while breastfeeding
options.C: Ovulation can happen before her monthly period returns
options.D: Hormonal contraceptives must start on delivery day

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn they can release an egg and get pregnant again before they even see their first postpartum period!

question: What is a great food tip for a mum dealing with early morning sickness?

options.A: Consuming a large, high-fat breakfast immediately upon waking
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of citrus juice on an empty stomach
options.C: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks like crackers before getting out of bed
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake throughout the entire day

explanation: Dry snacks help settle a restless morning tummy and gently boost blood sugar without triggering nausea.

question: Which layer of the outer adrenal gland (adrenal cortex) produces stress hormones like cortisol?

options.A: Zona glomerulosa
options.B: Zona reticularis
options.C: Adrenal medulla
options.D: Zona fasciculata

explanation: Think of the adrenal cortex layers from outside in as Salt, Sugar, Sex (Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis). The middle layer, zona fasciculata, handles the 'sugar' hormones like cortisol to help you cope with stress!

question: Why is it important to ask patients about traditional herbal remedies before giving hospital medications?

options.A: Herbal mixtures can interact dangerously with prescribed hospital medications
options.B: Traditional remedies cancel out the cost of hospital drugs
options.C: Doctors use herbal history to calculate exact body weight
options.D: Hospital management requires a complete inventory of home items

explanation: Many patients mix local herbs with hospital drugs. Asking helps you catch sneaky drug-herb reactions that could harm the patient.

question: A farm worker comes in with excessive drooling, tearing, sweating, and diarrhea after spraying crops. What type of poisoning is most likely?

options.A: Cholinergic
options.B: Sympathomimetic
options.C: Sedative-hypnotic
options.D: Anticholinergic

explanation: Fantastic clinical deduction! Organophosphate pesticides cause over-stimulation of the parasympathetic system—remember the helpful SLUDGE mnemonic for all those wet secretions!

question: Why are medications like gabapentin or amitriptyline prescribed for some types of chronic pain?

options.A: They act as fast rescue doses for sudden, unexpected pain spikes
options.B: They replace strong opioids so the patient never develops any tolerance
options.C: They are adjuvant drugs that help calm irritated nerves and unusual pain signals
options.D: They cure the underlying tissue damage that caused the discomfort

explanation: Adjuvants are medications developed for other purposes, such as seizures or depression, that prove very effective at treating nerve-related pain. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h6)

question: Why do dialogue groups involving village elders and men help improve women's health access?

options.A: They address cultural norms that restrict women from seeking care
options.B: They replace the professional nursing staff in maternal wards
options.C: They prevent women from leaving their homes for any reason
options.D: They give men exclusive control over clinic budgets and supplies

explanation: You got it! Since elders and men often hold decision-making power in the home, getting them on board helps remove cultural blocks that stop women from getting timely care.

question: What is the main goal of practicing medical asepsis (clean technique) on the ward?

options.A: To sterilize multi-use equipment between patients
options.B: To destroy all bacterial spores on the patient's skin
options.C: To reduce the number of pathogens and stop their spread
options.D: To create a completely germ-free surgical environment

explanation: You got it! Medical asepsis is all about reducing the number of germs and stopping them from traveling around the ward.

question: Why is custodial care considered different from skilled nursing care?

options.A: Skilled nursing care is strictly limited to helping patients eat meals.
options.B: Custodial care focuses on non-medical daily support rather than clinical treatments.
options.C: Custodial care can only be performed inside a licensed intensive care unit.
options.D: Skilled nursing care does not require any form of professional training.

explanation: Custodial care is meant for daily personal tasks, whereas skilled nursing involves medical procedures ordered by a physician and performed by licensed nurses. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the biggest benefit of having a reflex arc that goes through the spinal cord?

options.A: It lets you consciously analyze pain before you react
options.B: It gives a super fast, automatic reaction to protect your body from harm
options.C: It stops sensory messages from ever reaching the brain
options.D: It forces your brain to think carefully before any tiny movement

explanation: Brilliant! Reflexes skip the slow brain-thinking process so you can pull your hand away from a hot stove instantly before you get badly burned.

question: Which type of wound is created under clean, controlled hospital conditions?

options.A: Contaminated laceration
options.B: Traumatic abrasion
options.C: Intentional wound
options.D: Infected ulcer

explanation: An intentional wound is just a planned surgical cut made by a surgeon using strict sterile steps. Nice and straightforward!

question: Why is breaking the seal of a closed urinary drainage system a bad idea?

options.A: It stops urine production in the kidneys
options.B: It causes the retention balloon to deflate spontaneously
options.C: It changes the French size of the catheter tubing
options.D: It allows bacteria to enter the system and travel directly into the bladder

explanation: Keep that system closed! Breaking the seal opens a wide-open highway for germs to march straight up into the bladder.

question: Why is the home health nurse often described as the central communication hub?

options.A: They make all final medical diagnoses without consulting a physician
options.B: They are the only healthcare worker allowed to visit the residence
options.C: They manage the central telephone switchboard for the health agency
options.D: They connect the patient, family, doctors, and therapists together

explanation: Because nurses visit frequently, they coordinate information between all the different disciplines involved in the patient's care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why might a quiet, withdrawn patient still be dealing with serious fear?

options.A: Fear can cause behavioral withdrawal and freezing instead of crying out.
options.B: Withdrawn patients have completely empty minds.
options.C: Silence always proves that a patient is fully relaxed.
options.D: Quiet patients never experience the fight-or-flight response.

explanation: Well done! Not everyone screams or cries when scared. Some patients freeze, shut down, or go completely quiet when they are overwhelmed.

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is an ovarian cyst?

options.A: A solid tumor growing inside the uterus
options.B: A complete blockage of the vaginal canal
options.C: An infection of the fallopian tubes
options.D: A fluid-filled sac on or inside an ovary

explanation: Ovarian cysts are pockets or sacs filled with fluid that develop on or inside the ovarian tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h1)

question: Which condition makes the rectal route unsafe because of a high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Mild tension headache
options.B: Simple upper respiratory infection
options.C: Severe thrombocytopenia
options.D: Chronic ankle swelling

explanation: Low platelet counts mean any trauma to the rectal lining can lead to serious, hard-to-stop bleeding. You've got this!

question: Why must you check IV lines and power cords before adjusting a smart bed's position?

options.A: To prevent lines from becoming pinched or disconnected during articulation
options.B: To ensure the bed connects properly to the central hospital Wi-Fi
options.C: To prevent the bed's built-in scale from registering incorrect weights
options.D: To keep the floor clear so housekeeping can mop underneath

explanation: As the bed moves up or down, it can easily pull or snap tight IV lines and oxygen tubing if you haven't checked them first.

question: What is the primary underlying problem in all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion
options.B: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.C: Excessive carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Severe localized tissue trauma

explanation: Shock fundamentally happens when blood flow is insufficient to supply oxygen and nutrients to the body's tissues and organs. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h1)

question: What is one of the earliest signs that a patient is experiencing internal or external bleeding?

options.A: An immediate loss of consciousness
options.B: An increased heart rate and restlessness
options.C: Deep, slow breathing and pink warm skin
options.D: A very high and stable blood pressure

explanation: Tachycardia and mild anxiety are early warnings as adrenaline kicks in to compensate for lost blood volume. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why do public health nurses track family planning statistics?

options.A: To calculate exact hospital budgets for surgery
options.B: To punish communities with high birth rates
options.C: To replace direct physical assessment of patients
options.D: To track reproductive trends and measure health policies

explanation: Think of family planning stats as your community's report card! They help nurses and public health workers spot health trends and see if our policies are actually helping women and families.

question: According to global health bodies like the WHO, what is the official age bracket for adolescent pregnancy?

options.A: 8 to 15 years old
options.B: 10 to 19 years old
options.C: 15 to 25 years old
options.D: 12 to 21 years old

explanation: You got this! Health agencies classify adolescent pregnancy as any pregnancy occurring in females between 10 and 19 years old.

question: A clinical instructor tells students to use a case they saw last week to understand a new patient's symptoms. Which theory is this?

options.A: Classical conditioning
options.B: Constructivism
options.C: Rote memorization
options.D: Behaviorism

explanation: Constructivism means 'building' new knowledge on top of what you already know and experienced before. You've got this!

question: Which formula is used to calculate cardiac output?

options.A: Blood pressure divided by resistance
options.B: Stroke volume multiplied by heart rate
options.C: Stroke volume plus blood volume
options.D: Heart rate divided by stroke volume

explanation: Cardiac output is the product of how much blood is pumped per beat (stroke volume) and how many beats occur per minute (heart rate). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: Because a pregnant teenager's pelvis is still growing, she is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Obstructed labor
options.B: Chronic heart failure
options.C: Placental overgrowth
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: You're doing great! An immature pelvis may not be wide enough for the baby to pass through easily, raising the risk of obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: What happens to a woman's cervical mucus during her fertile window to help conception?

options.A: It becomes clear, stretchy, and slippery
options.B: It develops a foul odor and heavy discharge
options.C: It dries up completely to block germs
options.D: It turns thick, sticky, and brownish

explanation: High estrogen turns cervical mucus into a friendly, slippery highway that helps swimming sperm travel easily toward the egg. Nature is amazing!

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard emergency maneuver used during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: applying downward pressure above the maternal pubic bone
options.B: flexing the maternal legs sharply up toward her abdomen
options.C: administering strong uterine relaxants intravenously
options.D: summoning immediate pediatric and obstetric assistance

explanation: Spot on! For shoulder dystocia, we use physical repositioning (like the McRoberts maneuver) and suprapubic pressure rather than IV uterine relaxants.

question: What is the main goal of public health policies in government?

options.A: To stop foreign doctors from visiting
options.B: To close down all primary healthcare centers
options.C: To guide resource distribution and structure healthcare delivery
options.D: To make huge profits for drug manufacturing companies

explanation: Correct! Policies act like a roadmap. They give government agencies the rules and structure they need to organize, fund, and deliver healthcare properly.

question: A patient's tray is empty, but you suspect they didn't eat. What might have happened?

options.A: Food may have been eaten by a visitor or spilled
options.B: Dietary intake only counts if a dietitian sees it
options.C: The kitchen staff forgot to put food on the plate
options.D: The patient's metabolism is moving too fast

explanation: Correct! An empty tray doesn't guarantee the patient ate the food. Always double-check before charting their intake.

question: What three areas does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assess?

options.A: Blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature
options.B: Swallowing reflex, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Pain tolerance, mood, and cognitive memory

explanation: The GCS is a quick, reliable way to check a patient's level of consciousness by testing these three clear reactions.

question: As a nurse managing a cholera treatment camp, what is your most critical intervention for saving lives immediately?

options.A: Aggressive rehydration using oral rehydration salts and intravenous fluids
options.B: Strict isolation of patients in a dark, soundproofed room
options.C: Immediate quarantine of all healthy family members in their homes
options.D: Immediate administration of broad-spectrum topical skin ointments

explanation: Spot on! Cholera causes rapid, severe fluid loss, so replacing those fluids quickly with ORS and IV drips is the number one life-saving step.

question: How does understanding a client's cultural background improve psychosocial nursing care?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.
options.B: It allows the nurse to change the client's religious practices.
options.C: It proves which medical treatment is the only correct option.
options.D: It helps the nurse respect the client's beliefs about illness and healing.

explanation: Cultural awareness builds trust and ensures care plans align with the client's personal values and traditions. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h7)

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: What is a very common complaint you will hear from patients who have anaemia?

options.A: Chronic fatigue and shortness of breath
options.B: Uncontrolled involuntary muscle twitching
options.C: Sudden inability to move the left arm
options.D: Severe pain in the lower right abdomen

explanation: When red blood cells are low, they carry less oxygen. This leaves the body tissues starving for oxygen, causing constant tiredness and breathlessness.

question: What is a frequent cause of a false-positive Mantoux test in individuals from other countries?

options.A: Prior vaccination with the BCG vaccine
options.B: Having a severe viral cold during testing
options.C: Receiving the injection too deep in the skin
options.D: Taking daily multi-vitamin supplements

explanation: The BCG vaccine, given in many countries to prevent childhood TB, can cause the immune system to react to PPD, creating a false-positive skin test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: What is considered the single most effective habit to stop the spread of infection?

options.A: Changing hospital scrubs hourly
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gloves all day
options.D: Using strong chemical sprays

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using alcohol rub) at the right moments is your absolute best defense against spreading germs!

question: During a family consultation, a mother yells at her teenage daughter for missing doses of her asthma inhaler. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Agree with the mother that the teenager is being irresponsible and lazy.
options.B: Intervene to calm the environment and encourage calm dialogue between them.
options.C: Ask the mother to leave the room permanently so she cannot return.
options.D: Give the teenager a stern warning about the dangers of severe asthma attacks.

explanation: Nurses must de-escalate tension and model constructive communication to help families work through conflicts safely. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of health education in schools?

options.A: Training every child to become a professional nurse
options.B: Reducing the budget allocated for school feeding
options.C: Empowering students to make healthy choices independently
options.D: Eliminating the need for any physical education classes

explanation: Health education equips children with the knowledge and attitudes needed to practice healthy habits on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: What delicate structure separates the right and left lateral ventricles from each other?

options.A: Septum pellucidum
options.B: Cerebral aqueduct
options.C: Corpus callosum
options.D: Choroid plexus

explanation: Well done! The septum pellucidum is a thin, thin wall that sits right down the middle, separating the two lateral ventricles.

question: Why would you give a drug through an injection (parenterally) instead of having the patient swallow it?

options.A: It requires no special technical skill.
options.B: It achieves much faster drug absorption.
options.C: It is completely painless for the patient.
options.D: It has zero risk of local tissue damage.

explanation: You got this! Injections bypass the digestive system straight into the bloodstream or tissues, meaning the medicine gets to work much quicker.

question: Why is the hypodermis so important for protecting your bones and muscles?

options.A: It contains active stem cells that repair bone fractures
options.B: It acts as a physical shock absorber against trauma
options.C: It generates sweat to cool deep tissues during exercise
options.D: It produces keratin to harden the surface against impacts

explanation: Spot on! The layer of fat cushions bumps and blows, protecting the delicate muscles and bones underneath.

question: Which imaging test is best for getting a clear view of bone structures in the sinuses and ears?

options.A: Routine chest X-ray
options.B: Surface skin ultrasound
options.C: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

explanation: CT scans are fantastic at imaging hard bone, making them the top choice for looking at sinus walls and inner ear details.

question: Why does the baby's head usually rotate internally as it moves down through the pelvis?

options.A: to signal the placenta that it is time to detach from the uterine wall
options.B: to fit the widest part of the head through the widest diameter of the pelvic outlet
options.C: to prevent the umbilical cord from wrapping tightly around the fetal neck
options.D: to decrease the intensity of maternal uterine contractions

explanation: Correct! The pelvis has specific shapes, and the baby rotates to match those contours for a smoother passage through the birth canal.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand a patient's living situation and financial stability?

options.A: They determine the exact surgical approach needed for recovery
options.B: They replace the need to conduct a review of body systems
options.C: Insurances require this data to calculate daily calorie counts
options.D: These factors directly affect the ability to follow medical treatments

explanation: Spot on! If money is tight or housing is unstable, buying prescriptions or returning for follow-ups can be a massive hurdle.

question: How does long-term high blood pressure change the structure of the heart muscle over time?

options.A: It cures high blood pressure by strengthening the valves
options.B: It repairs damaged arteries and restores normal blood flow
options.C: It changes the shape and thickness of the heart muscle, leading to weak pumping
options.D: It shrinks the heart chambers back to normal sizes

explanation: Just like lifting heavy weights builds your biceps, fighting high pressure makes the heart walls thicken and change shape, which eventually wears it out.

question: Why are sugary carbonated drinks a poor choice for everyday hydration in teens?

options.A: They contain too much pure protein for growing kidneys.
options.B: They instantly cause permanent tooth decay on first contact.
options.C: They lower body temperature to dangerous levels.
options.D: They cause blood sugar spikes and do not hydrate efficiently.

explanation: Too much sugar slows down how fast the stomach empties liquids, meaning sugary drinks don't quench thirst or hydrate as well as plain water.

question: A young woman who had FGM as a child comes to your clinic with painful periods and trouble passing urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A newly developed hormonal imbalance
options.B: An acute bacterial kidney infection
options.C: Scar tissue buildup and urethral obstruction
options.D: Normal physiological changes of aging

explanation: Years of healing leave tough scar tissue that can block the urinary and vaginal openings, making both urination and menstruation very painful.

question: Why is the very first cell division in oogenesis uneven or asymmetric?

options.A: Only the smaller cell is capable of surviving outside the ovary
options.B: One daughter cell keeps almost all the cytoplasm while the other becomes a tiny polar body
options.C: The cell divides without copying its DNA properly
options.D: Both daughter cells end up with different numbers of chromosomes

explanation: Think of it as sharing resources wisely. The egg keeps almost all the cytoplasm and nutrients, while the waste genetic material goes into a tiny polar body.

question: What is the typical average length of a complete ovarian cycle?

options.A: 28 days
options.B: 40 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 7 days

explanation: A standard text-book ovarian cycle is calculated to last about twenty-eight days, though normal variations among women are very common. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: A mum on tocolytics says her chest feels tight and she's struggling to breathe. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Document the findings as a normal side effect
options.B: Stop the medication infusion and notify the doctor
options.C: Encourage the patient to take deep and slow breaths
options.D: Increase the intravenous fluid rate immediately

explanation: Patient safety first! Chest tightness can point to dangerous fluid overload (pulmonary edema) from tocolytics, so your best move is stopping the infusion right away and calling the doctor.

question: A diabetic patient is stressed because they cannot afford their monthly insulin. Who should the nurse involve first?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Surgical specialist
options.C: Social worker
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: Brilliant! Social workers are absolute rockstars at connecting patients with financial aid and community assistance programs.

question: If a client reports mild, normal side effects from her contraceptive, which action is NOT helpful?

options.A: Dismissing their concerns as imaginary
options.B: Providing reassurance and timeline expectations
options.C: Validating their physical experience
options.D: Explaining simple ways to manage the symptoms

explanation: Never brush off a client's feelings! Listening, validating, and supporting them builds trust and helps them stick to their care.

question: Which factor contributes most directly to delays in treating obstetric emergencies?

options.A: Needing permission from family members before seeking care
options.B: Excessive availability of ambulance services in rural areas
options.C: Early registration for routine antenatal care
options.D: Having too many nurses on duty at the primary health center

explanation: When a woman lacks decision-making power, waiting for authorization from male or elderly relatives causes dangerous delays during emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h3)

question: Which of these conditions is best treated with a warm compress?

options.A: An acute, newly sprained wrist with severe swelling
options.B: An active nosebleed from the nasal septum
options.C: A painful muscle spasm in the lower back
options.D: A fresh surgical incision with active oozing

explanation: Warmth helps tight, cramped muscles relax and brings fresh blood flow to soothe stiffness.

question: How fast do the intense symptoms of a sudden gout attack usually peak?

options.A: Gradually across a full year
options.B: Within 12 to 24 hours
options.C: Right after finishing a heavy meal
options.D: Over several weeks to months

explanation: That's right! Gout attacks come on fast and furious, usually hitting their most painful peak within just half a day to a full day.

question: What is the usual recommended length of time to take nitrofurantoin for a simple bladder infection?

options.A: Twenty-one days
options.B: Fourteen days
options.C: A single dose
options.D: Five days

explanation: A short, sweet 5-day course is usually all it takes to clear a simple bladder infection while keeping side effects low.

question: What does client-centered care primarily turn the patient into?

options.A: An active partner in their own health decisions
options.B: A primary financial contributor to the ward
options.C: An unofficial clinical researcher
options.D: An independent supervisor of hospital staff

explanation: Client-centered care values the patient's voice, making them an active participant alongside the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction is totally predictable because it depends directly on the dose?

options.A: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.B: Type A reaction
options.C: Type B reaction
options.D: Allergic reaction

explanation: Type A reactions happen because the drug's normal action is just too strong. Because they are dose-related, they are easy to predict!

question: Why is dragging a patient straight across bedsheets a bad idea for their skin?

options.A: It completely blocks the production of natural skin oils
options.B: It forces moisture deep into the subcutaneous fat layer
options.C: It creates friction and shear forces that damage skin and blood vessels
options.D: It causes an immediate drop in the patient's systemic blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Pulling someone across rough sheets creates friction and tears tiny blood vessels underneath. Always lift, never drag!

question: Which blood test is more specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Lipase
options.C: Creatinine
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Spot on! Serum lipase is the go-to test because it's much more specific to the pancreas than amylase, and it stays elevated longer during an attack.

question: Where does the federal VAPP Act automatically apply right after being signed?

options.A: Lagos State only
options.B: All thirty-six states simultaneously
options.C: Rural communities only
options.D: Federal Capital Territory, Abuja

explanation: Correct! The federal VAPP Act applies directly in the FCT. For other states, their local houses of assembly have to 'domesticate' it first.

question: What is widely known as the biggest challenge facing drug safety systems around the world?

options.A: Underreporting of adverse drug reactions
options.B: Too many digital reporting applications
options.C: Immediate withdrawal of safe medications
options.D: An excess of trained clinical investigators

explanation: Spot on! Many busy clinicians forget or fail to report side effects, meaning most mild or moderate reactions go completely undocumented.

question: What is anticipatory grief?

options.A: Anger directed at doctors after a misdiagnosis
options.B: Depression caused by a sudden physical injury
options.C: Grief experienced before the actual death occurs
options.D: Relief felt when a patient finally passes away

explanation: Anticipatory grief is the mourning process that happens prior to an expected death as losses accumulate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: What is the maximum score for the verbal (talking) category in a fully alert adult?
explanation: The verbal score ranges from 1 to 5. Scoring a 5 means your patient is fully alert and oriented to time, place, and person.

question: What action officially marks the start time of a 24-hour urine collection test?

options.A: Having the patient empty their bladder and discarding that urine
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of water right before the test starts
options.C: Saving the very first morning urine sample in the collection jug
options.D: Collecting all urine produced starting from midnight regardless of sleep

explanation: To get an accurate 24-hour count, we start with a totally empty bladder so we don't accidentally count old urine that sat in the body overnight!

question: Why might a patient with a degenerative nerve disease be given an antidepressant along with their other medications?

options.A: Coping with a life-changing chronic illness often takes a heavy emotional toll
options.B: Sadness is the physical cause of nerve cell breakdown
options.C: Depression medications help the liver process other pills faster
options.D: Antidepressants act as a direct cure for muscle weakness

explanation: Spot on! Caring for the whole person means looking after their mind as well as their body. Chronic illnesses are tough emotionally, and good mental health support is a vital part of nursing care.

question: Why does a person feel breathless when there is a mismatch in breathing signals?

options.A: The brain gets confused because the effort of trying to breathe doesn't match how the lungs actually move.
options.B: The brainstem shuts down ventilation to conserve oxygen.
options.C: The diaphragm relaxes completely and refuses to contract further.
options.D: The heart pumps too much blood to the lungs, causing fluid overload.

explanation: Breathlessness happens when the brain's command to breathe doesn't match the actual movement of the chest wall. Simple and clear!

question: Which communication pattern involves all team members talking freely with one another without a strict central bottleneck?

options.A: Y-pattern network
options.B: All-channel network
options.C: Wheel network
options.D: Chain network

explanation: An all-channel communication network allows open, multi-directional sharing of information among all members of the group. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h4)

question: What should a nurse do if they find out a young girl in the community is about to undergo FGM?

options.A: Wait until the procedure is finished before offering any medical help
options.B: Report the threat to child protection authorities in line with legal frameworks
options.C: Advise the parents on how to find a clean, sterile cutter
options.D: Keep the information completely secret to respect family traditions

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you have both a legal and moral duty to protect minors from harm and report any planned FGM to the appropriate authorities.

question: Which skin gland makes an oily substance called sebum to keep your hair and skin soft?

options.A: Ceruminous gland
options.B: Apocrine gland
options.C: Sebaceous gland
options.D: Eccrine gland

explanation: Correct! Sebaceous glands are our natural oil producers, keeping our skin waterproofed and conditioned.
